## Purpose

This notebook documents the analytical role of `R/core.R` in a research pipeline. It explains each function as a methodological block: configuration control, data integrity constraints, feature construction, model fitting, prediction generation, and evaluation metrics.

## Setup

```{r}
# Load core dependencies required for the full workflow.
# We explicitly load these libraries in the notebook to mirror execution assumptions in the target pipeline.
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(yaml)

# Source project functions.
source("R/core.R")
```

## 1) Configuration loading and contract checks

```{r}
# The config object is the single source of truth for input paths.
# Academic reproducibility depends on parameterizing paths rather than hardcoding them across scripts.
cfg <- load_config("config/config.yml")
str(cfg)
```

## 2) Data ingestion

```{r}
# Data ingestion is intentionally thin: this function should be deterministic and side-effect free.
# Any schema or quality assumptions are enforced in validation, not in read-time heuristics.
raw_data <- load_input_data(cfg)
raw_data
```

## 3) Validation and assumptions

```{r}
# Validation enforces minimum inferential assumptions:
#  - required predictors/outcome present
#  - sufficient row count for model fitting
#  - numeric typing for model terms
#  - no missing values in required fields
valid_data <- validate_input_data(raw_data)
valid_data
```

## 4) Feature engineering

```{r}
# Feature expansion adds a polynomial term x^2.
# This is a simple nonlinear approximation strategy often used as a baseline before richer models.
features <- prepare_features(valid_data)
features
```

## 5) Baseline model estimation

```{r}
# OLS with a quadratic term balances interpretability and flexibility.
# In production research, one would compare this against alternatives using time-aware validation.
model <- fit_baseline_model(features)
summary(model)
```

## 6) Prediction and metric construction

```{r}
# Predictions are generated on the same feature set in this baseline example.
# Metrics are in-sample and should not be interpreted as out-of-sample generalization quality.
predictions <- generate_predictions(model, features)
metrics <- compute_metrics(predictions)

predictions
metrics
```

## 7) End-to-end orchestration

```{r}
# The orchestration helper is useful for clean API boundaries and integration tests.
# It executes all stages and returns named artifacts for downstream inspection.
out <- run_nowcast_pipeline("config/config.yml")
names(out)
out$metrics
```
